correctness.rationale: At the assigned frozen 10-file tree, all 15 Petersen edges are defined as GP(5,2), and each face is exactly an edge mask excluding all k-edge matchings for k=2..5. An independent Python reconstruction enumerated all 75/145/90/6 forbidden matchings, 56/1073/8558/27449 augmented faces and 24/530/4271/13720 toggle pairs, then oriented and topologically sorted every 105/3990/47085/194040 Hasse incidence with no cycles. It independently recovered the exact critical CW cell dimensions and signed integer Morse matrices. For k=3 the lone 4-to-3 column is primitive; for k=4 the 8x5 6-to-5 matrix has rank four and a determinant +1 maximal minor, with 7-to-6 primitive column spanning its kernel; for k=5 the 10-to-9 column is primitive. The CW models have one vertex and no lower positive cells. Standard Morse CW, Hurewicz, and homological Whitehead give the claimed integral wedge homotopy types, not just mod-two Betti groups. For k=2 six critical 1-cells are loops; for k>=6 no matching fits ten vertices and the full simplex is contractible. Distinct positive homology degrees at consecutive k and final contractibility prove the four unit-length persistence bars. Source tree hash was reconstructed as an actual Git tree from all ten returned blob identities and agrees exactly with assignment.

evidence: Linusson–Shareshian–Welker Theorem 1.1 (arXiv:math/0410345, p.2), and Theorem 1.4 (p.3): full sphere wedges for complete graphs K_n and complete bipartite graphs K_{r,s}.

Shan–Lu–Wang Theorem 2.1 / Corollary 2.3 (arXiv:2609.02621v2, pp.4–5): homology injection and Leray equality restricted to bipartite graphs; the Petersen graph is nonbipartite.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the smallest canonical vertex-transitive nonbipartite cubic graph, and the matching-number bounded edge-subset filtration is natural and complete rather than an arbitrary selected threshold. The k=4 integral Morse attaching matrix and primitive lattice calculation and the k=5 high-dimensional wedge resolve nontrivial topology not provided by the prior known k=3 stage or general Leray bounds. The full sequence 6 S^1, 9 S^3, 4 S^5, 5 S^9 and exact integral persistence is a self-contained benchmark for graph-complex topology and future equivariant comparisons. No downstream theorem, arbitrary graph family, or general cubic classification is claimed; narrow complete finite exact results are valuable when the object/invariant are natural and not fully tabulated already.

final_claim: For the Petersen graph P=GP(5,2), the bounded-matching edge-subset complexes NM_k(P)={F⊆E(P):ν(F)<k} have integral homotopy types ∨^6 S^1 (k=2), ∨^9 S^3 (k=3; already published on 2026-10-18), ∨^4 S^5 (k=4), ∨^5 S^9 (k=5), and are contractible for k≥6; the complete positive-degree integral matching-threshold persistence has six [2,3) degree-1, nine [3,4) degree-3, four [4,5) degree-5, and five [5,6) degree-9 bars. For k=1 only the empty simplex occurs (empty ordinary realization).
limitations: The k=3 wedge is not new: exact 2026-10-18 published result with stronger S_5 symmetry. The surviving originality of the complete theorem rests on the exact k=4 and k=5 integral stages and filtration, not on all four being new.
The k=2 stage is elementary; lack of a separate earlier matching-number table does not by itself establish originality.
Finite exhaustive reconstruction certifies only this graph and thresholds. It is a legitimate exact finite proof, not a general-graph or equivariant classification.
No universal novelty assertion: potential unindexed Petersen nonmatching graph homotopy or general theorem remains an originality risk.
